title: Per-token latency signature + cache spectral attribution
creator: Amina Park
description: Motivation: We need a consistent, low-overhead signal that attributes per-request latency to token-level phases (tokenization, model forward, KV cache retrieval, kernel execution, post-processing) and quantifies the latency delta from cache hits vs cache misses. This ticket designs and implements a lightweight per-token timing signature, integrates it into tracing hooks, and pumps an aggregated "cache spectral" metric into the metrics pipeline for dashboarding and alerting.
acceptance_criteria: Per-token timing hooks instrumented in the serving hot path with <5% p99 request overhead in canary workload
KV cache hit/miss annotated on token spans and surfaced in traces (jaeger-compatible) and logs
Aggregated cache spectral metric (percentiles by token position and sequence length) emitted to metrics pipeline every minute
New dashboard widgets for token-level latency heatmap and cache delta distribution added to Console
End-to-end tests and a small benchmark harness (synthetic and real workload) demonstrating meaningful cost attribution improvements compared to baseline
comments: 2026-02-18 - Amina Park: Initial ticket created after incident-run analysis showed unexplained p99 regression on long-context routes. See notes in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Token+Latency+Investigation

2026-02-20 - Diego Alvarez: Spike completed to measure hook overhead. Prototype added token-timestamp insertion points at: pre-tokenize, post-tokenize, pre-forward, post-kv-lookup, post-forward, post-emit. Observed ~3% median CPU increase and ~6% p99 tail in a synthetic single-tenant canary. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/9821

2026-02-24 - Feedback (SRE): Need to ensure telemetry is sampled or aggregated before shipping; cannot increase cardinality beyond token position + sequence-length buckets. Recommendation: emit 'cache_spectral' histogram with labeled buckets for hit/miss and token-position-range.

2026-02-28 - Design decision: Use lightweight 16-bit timestamp counters (relative to request start) to reduce serialization size. Token spans will not include full payloads; only timing delta, position, and cache flag. Traces will use sampling=0.1 by default and full aggregation will go to metrics via an out-of-band summarizer.

2026-03-03 - Implementation note: Added summarizer service to runtime edge that consumes token timing batches and emits aggregated metrics (percentiles, hit/miss deltas) to Prometheus pushgateway. Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/307 - currently behind feature flag 'token_latency_signatures'.

2026-03-08 - Benchmarks: Canary run against real production-like traffic (1000 rps, mixture of chat and long-context) shows metric summarizer adds <1% additional CPU at tail instances and network overhead ~120 KB/s. Measured that cache hit reduces per-token median latency by ~2.4ms and p95 by ~7.6ms on long sequences (>=2048 tokens).

2026-03-10 - PM review (Jaya Patel): Dashboard mockups approved. Need rollout plan: enable tracing hooks only for dedicated and hosted tier beta customers initially, collect 2 weeks of data, then evaluate defaults for self-serve users.
2026-03-12 - Security review (K. Morgan): No sensitive user content included in traces. Confirmed that token payload is not serialized. KMS audit ok. Marked security_review_required=false.
Next steps: finish end-to-end tests, add dashboard panels in Console, schedule canary rollout for 2026-03-18, and follow up with cost analysis to present at Infra sync.
